title: Streaming retry idempotency: prevent half-counted stream tokens across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Several customers reported billing discrepancies tied to streaming responses where tokens were ~50% undercounted for a subset of streaming reconnect flows. The issue appears only when clients reconnect streaming sessions (same stream id) across different deployment types (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) or when requests route through the new batching/kv-cache fastpath. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigation, and fix rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming generation (chat) on Hosted with client stream_id X and request long output (>= 150 tokens).
2) Mid-stream, force a network disconnect from the client (SIGINT or drop connection).
3) Immediately retry by reconnecting with the same stream_id X; ensure request is routed to a different pool (Dedicated or Private) or to a node behind the new batching fastpath.
4) Observe tokens billed in metering ledger vs. actual tokens emitted by the final stream.
investigation_notes: Observed pattern: first partial fragment consumes tokens and writes a KV cache prefix. Retry requests sometimes read the prefix but the accounting path treated the resumed fragments as 'continuation' and only billed deltas when a cache hit occurred, but the cache-hit path occasionally skipped the final accounting write leading to ~half-counted tokens.
Issue reproducible in staging when routing policy forces cross-deployment failover; not reproduced when both attempts land on same node or same pool with consistent routing metadata.

Trace logs show accounting RPC acknowledged by serving runtime but accounting-aggregator service didn't receive the idempotency marker due to a race when cache->response path short-circuited response emission before accounting flush.
Related subsystems: streaming runtime, KV prefix cache fastpath (opt-batch-2), request router (smart-routing), and metering-aggregator's idempotency dedupe table.
root_cause: A race between the optimized streaming fastpath (which emits cached prefixes and then short-circuits response assembly) and the accounting flush path. When a retry hits a different pool, the fastpath emits tokens using a cache-hit shortcut that did not reliably write the idempotency key to the metering-aggregator before response completion. Subsequent aggregator rollups missed those writes and only counted resumed tokens, resulting in undercounting.
impact: High billing undercount for affected customers; multiple enterprise customers submitted escalations with potential revenue leakage. A subset of long-running streaming sessions (>=100 tokens) that experienced mid-stream reconnects are affected. Impacts both Hosted customers and those using Dedicated/Private when cross-pool routing occurs (regional failover, warm-pool routing).
customers_affected: Unknown set of customers using long streaming workloads; we estimate ~0.4% of streaming sessions during incident window
mitigation: 1) Hotfix deployed: force accounting flush on streaming completion path before response short-circuiting (hotfix patch runtime v1.21.3-hotfix). Deployed to Hosted and Dedicated warm pools 2026-03-06 18:00 UTC.
2) Temporarily disable opt-batch-2 KV cache fastpath for cross-pool routed streams via safe-flag (safeflag: disable-kv-fastpath-crosspool) until full fix validated.

3) Backfilled missing idempotency markers: run reconciliation job to detect sessions with emitted tokens but missing aggregator entries and re-ingest accounting writes based on request traces (reconciliation job id reconc-2026-03-07).
4) Customer communication: PM outreach to escalated accounts with timeline and interim refunds/credits where applicable.
permanent_fix_plan: A) Add atomic accounting write at the earliest emission boundary for cached-prefix emissions so every emitted token fragment is tied to an idempotency key persisted before any short-circuit return.
B) Harden metering-aggregator to accept out-of-order writes and reconcile by session id + sequence, with idempotency TTL longer for streaming sessions.
C) Add e2e integration tests that simulate cross-pool streaming reconnects and validate accounting consistency across Hosted/Dedicated/Private routing scenarios.
D) Roll out runtime-1.22 with the accounting atomicity change and aggregator reconciliation improvements; plan staged rollout with canary, 25%, 50%, 100% over two days.
E) Post-deploy: run targeted backfill and re-run billing reconciliation checks for impacted billing periods.
notes: 2026-03-05: Customer Acme Analytics reported a 48% token gap for a specific long-running stream; support collected request_ids and traces.
2026-03-06: Reproduced in staging; hotfix prepared and merged; hotfix deployed to Hosted evening canary and immediately mitigated new occurrences.
2026-03-07: Reconciliation job run; preliminary backfill re-ingested ~73% of missing accounting entries for sample of affected sessions.
2026-03-09: PMs notified customers and issued credits where backfill confirmed; some customers requested detailed postmortem which is being drafted.
2026-03-12: Permanent fix PR opened and initial review comments by Talia Barnes and Omar Chen.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New e2e tests validate that for streaming retry across pools, metering-aggregator ledger matches emitted tokens for sampled sessions.
2) runtime-1.22 canary shows zero regression in latency and no new undercount occurrences in 48h canary window.
3) Reconciliation job confirms backfilled entries and billing reconciliation reports drop below 0.01% variance for streaming flows.
4) Customer-facing postmortem published and affected customers confirmed credits or reconciled invoices.
